https://atomicdata.dev/properties/descri: Where this integration's source can be fetched from, for entries not bundled as a local package.json in this folder. Optional — omitted for integrations developed in this repo.

The version of this integration currently published in this repository, mirrored from its package.json (see integrations/README.md). Omitted for an entry with no local package.json, such as one reached through the generic LocalThought/Devonian bridge or fetched from pluginUrl. A host compares this against what an installation has pinned to offer an update.

What this plugin needs from the node, derived from its manifest and never written by hand: a sorted JSON array such as ["persistent-host", "plugin-routes:read-only", "public-origin", "wasm-sandbox"], with `plugin-routes:<level>`, `operator-listener:<name>` and `operator-sidecar:<name>` for the gated surfaces of docs/design/server-plugin-routes.md section 0. The same list the host puts on each /plugin-catalog entry (atomic-server#1732), so a client can compare it with the node's `hostFeatures` without parsing manifests. Required on the entry of a package whose manifest is version 3 or needs the plugin-routes feature; integrations/tooling/catalog-requires.mjs checks it and writes it.

URL of the built ES module for exactly this entry's `version`, which a host installs as a drive app's entry point. Distinct from `pluginUrl`, which links to source. For an app built in this repo it is `https://ontola.github.io/atomic-plugins/apps/<shortname>/<version>/ui.js`: `integrations/<shortname>/app/build.mjs`'s output, committed at `apps/<shortname>/<version>/ui.js` and served by GitHub Pages from `main`. A version file on `main` is never changed or deleted, so a changed build needs a new version. A relative URL resolves against this catalog's own URL. See integrations/README.md, 'Publishing a drive app'.

Subresource Integrity hash (`sha384-` plus base64) of the `app-module` bytes. A host refuses to install or update from a module that does not match. `integrations/tooling/apps.mjs check` keeps it equal to the committed module and to a fresh build.
What one row in the installed app's table is called, singular (for example 'Pet'). Optional; the app may rename it itself.
What the installed app's table and its rows are called, plural (for example 'Pets'). Optional; given together with `app-row-name`.
